consumer: condition.cpp set_has_item's lambda (the u_has_item/npc_has_item dialogue/condition predicate) asking 'does the avatar possess a knife_combat?'
scope: only the character's own carried items (wielded/worn/inventory on-person), as charges_of + has_amount evaluate over the actor itself
decisive_source: src/condition.cpp::conditional_t<T>::set_has_item — returns actor->charges_of(item_id) > 0 || actor->has_amount(item_id, 1), the engine-computed yes/no possession predicate over the character actor
divergence: avatar holds the knife_combat inside a closed non-gun/non-magazine container in inventory: has_amount/charges_of (via visit_items) descends into container contents and returns true, but a shortcut that only scanned top-level wielded/worn/inventory entries (or the flat carried_items array) would wrongly report not-carrying
